title: Identity and pasting equations for exchange
statement:
Use the inverse images $u^{-1}$ on the bounded below derived categories of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], the derived direct images $Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] with the adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], the composition and identity isomorphisms $c^D_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$, $e^D_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ of the inverse images [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], and the composition isomorphisms $d^D_{u,v}:R(u\circ v)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*\circ Rv_*$ of the derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-composition]. For a cartesian square $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, let $\Ex_\square:g^{-1}Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ be the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Outer rectangles of pasted cartesian squares are cartesian squares [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. Then, as natural transformations of functors between bounded below derived categories:

1. (Identity square.) For $f:X\to Y$ and the square $\square_f=(f,f,\mathrm{id}_Y,\mathrm{id}_X)$,
$$
 Rf_*(e^D_X)\circ\Ex_{\square_f}=e^D_{Y}Rf_*:\ \mathrm{id}_Y^{-1}Rf_*\longrightarrow Rf_*,
$$
i.e. $\Ex_{\square_f}$ is the identity of $Rf_*$ once $\mathrm{id}^{-1}$ is identified with the identity functor by $e^D$.
2. (Horizontal pasting, composing the base changes.) For $\square_1=(f,f',g,g')$ and a cartesian square $\square_2=(f',f'',h,h')$ with $h:Y''\to Y'$, $h':X''\to X'$, $f'':X''\to Y''$, the outer rectangle $\square_2\cdot\square_1=(f,f'',g\circ h,g'\circ h')$ satisfies
$$
 \Ex_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}=(Rf''_*c^D_{g',h'})\circ(\Ex_{\square_2}g'^{-1})\circ(h^{-1}\Ex_{\square_1})\circ((c^D_{g,h})^{-1}Rf_*):
$$
$$
 (gh)^{-1}Rf_*\to h^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*\to h^{-1}Rf'_*g'^{-1}\to Rf''_*h'^{-1}g'^{-1}\to Rf''_*(g'h')^{-1}.
$$
3. (Vertical pasting, composing the direct images.) For $\square_1$ as above and a cartesian square $\square_3=(e,e',g',g'')$ with $e:W\to X$, $e':W'\to X'$, $g'':W'\to W$, the outer rectangle $\square_1\circ\square_3=(f\circ e,f'\circ e',g,g'')$ satisfies
$$
 \Ex_{\square_1\circ\square_3}=((d^D_{f',e'})^{-1}g''^{-1})\circ(Rf'_*\Ex_{\square_3})\circ(\Ex_{\square_1}Re_*)\circ(g^{-1}d^D_{f,e}):
$$
$$
 g^{-1}R(fe)_*\to g^{-1}Rf_*Re_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}Re_*\to Rf'_*Re'_*g''^{-1}\to R(f'e')_*g''^{-1}.
$$

proof.text: Apply the existing source identity pasting theorem to the commutative square underlying `IsPullback.id_horiz f`; its statement is exactly the first conjunct after unfolding `A`.

For horizontal pasting, apply the existing source theorem `derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_paste_horiz` to `sq₁.toCommSq`, `sq₂.toCommSq`, and `(sq₂.paste_horiz sq₁).toCommSq`. The generated associators and composition isomorphisms are definitionally the target expression.

Identify the project definition `derivedDirectImageComposition` with the generic bounded-below right-derived composition isomorphism. Unfolding it reduces the forward component to a conjugate. The `conjugateEquiv_eq_of_unit` criterion proves the inverse component equality from `derivedPlus_unit_comp_upperStarCompDerivedPlus`; the forward equality follows by cancellation with the generic composition isomorphism.

Apply the existing source theorem `derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_paste_vert` to the two commutative squares and their pasted square. Rewrite both occurrences of the generic composition isomorphism using the identification above and unfold `rightDerivedLowerStarPlus`; the result is the third conjunct exactly.

split_report.summary: Statement made precise: the identity law with the identity isomorphisms e^D of the derived inverse images, horizontal pasting (Stacks 0E47, composing the base changes, with c^D) and vertical pasting (Stacks 0E46, composing the direct images, with c^D and the derived direct-image composition isomorphisms d^D, defined as conjugates of c^D as in Stacks 0D6E); stmt_deps rewritten. The imported one-paragraph proof is replaced by four steps from the mate calculus: the dictionary Ex = mate of theta^D (definition), and for each law the corresponding pasting law of theta^D (new node lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-pasting) transported by the Mathlib mate lemmas (new leaf lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting: mateEquiv_vcomp, mateEquiv_hcomp, mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp, conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp, conjugateEquiv_id) and the whiskering lemma (new node lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker, not in Mathlib). The citation of lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-replacement is dropped: with Ex defined as the mate it is a pointer (it concerns the computation on resolutions, not used here). New: lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition (c^D, e^D and coherence; lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition has no associativity clause), def-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-composition, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate (leaf). lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-coherence (same unit, imported) states the same pasting laws plus resolution independence: merge candidate.
